results.title: A place to ponder upon the ultimate reality of life
results.text: Pashupati nath temple is the highly regarded Hindu temple of Shiva by all Hindus round the world. The temple itself is one of the ancient temple in the Kathmandu city. Although the entrance inside the temple premises is restricted to Hindus only but the ancient architect of the old structures can be observed while walking around outside the temple. The crematorium at the bank of the holy Bagmati is regarded as powerful place for performing the death ritual and cremation after death. Watching the rituals and the process of cremation from the other side of Bagmati river and by contemplating on the truth of own's life, which is impermanent by nature will give you insight that it is worthless to lead a life suppressed   anger, greed, hatred and aversion.

results.title: Profound experience you MUST see
results.text:
Is there anything better than seeing bodies of deceased family members being lovingly washed before being burnt & ashes scattered in their religious river? It sounds morbid, but - it's an experience you just have to witness to see the love. 

Painting a picture of the complex - naked boys backflipping into the religious river, cheeky monkeys stealing dry biscuits, discourteous Holy Men charging for photos from tourists, pleasant women blessing visitors with red rice Tilak Blessings, Tourists wandering around wondering where they can spend their hard earnt Holiday Dollars & loving family members watching on as their loved ones are washed & burnt. 

It's a memorable experience that'll burn deep in your soul.

results.title: Old and Pporly maintained
results.text: It breaks my heart to say this but this place could have been far better maintained and managed. Being such an old place of Hindu worship, I expected this to be a bit cleaner and a bit tidy probably. Anyway it is still worth a visit. It is better to carry something to cover your nose from time to time as the smells can sometimes be exhilarating.

results.title: An ancient temple but not maintained well
results.text: I went in with a lot o excitement knowing that many claims this as the largest Hindu temple of the world and is itself a World Heritage site. I was almost shocked at seeing how poor-managed the entire place was. Even if I try to keep the smell aside, the things spread here and there just makes it sad. Whether or not the world's largest, I assume this temple could use a much better cleaning from the Nepalese government.

results.title: Dirty and chaotic
results.text:
My wife and I were really surprised to see how filthy and chaotic everything there is.   The Buddhist temples were for the most part very well maintained and clean,  not the Hindu temples,  and this one was no different.   I went to use the free toilet there and it was filthy beyond and description.   

Of course we are glad we went due to it's historical value,  we decided not to go inside as there is plenty to see from the outside,  but,  it's really a huge culture shock.

results.title: learn to live watching death around you
results.text:
Probably you should be here to know the bitter truth of your own life. You feel heart pounding, when you see dead pure bodies lying and getting burnt. Smokes along with red flames grows to the sky and you feel the reality, keep pondering silently about your activities. You calculate your behaviours, your opinions,your moves and your attitudes. Sit opposite to the cremation sites alone and sit silently for an hour. You can see your body burning and but only your soul intact with you. Then and there probably you could feel the time you spent recklessly without any calculation. 
 The main objective of life i gurantee you that you will learn: live peacefully and let live other peacefully.
 I have learnt : No worries in life because everything goes and fades by time. Your loved ones may leave you. but you will have your soul. So nevery try to pollute it
 Other materialistic things like sculptures depicted on wooden wall and stones are awesome..... Try to find the meaning once you see it ..... google it and you will have knowldege real field trip knowledge. 
Dont do: donot try to feed monkeys otherwise they wont leave you
If you want to feed them just watch how experienced local people do that.
 Love animal but donot make them dependent on peoples offerings.
You need a whole day minimum to look around. Go and look in every corner of place because there are so many untouched corners where you get great arts.

results.title: Very very interesting!
results.text: If you travel in Nepal, it's a must-visit place. You will see how Nepalis think about their life and death. It might even change how you see things in your life!

results.title: A worthwhile experience - plan to spend a bit of time
results.text:
I was glad I heard a lot about the Temple and Crematoria before I went along since, even with the background knowledge I found it a quite confronting experience. 

The temple itself is off limits to non Hindus. 

I found the most interesting part of the visit was the banks of the river where the cremations take place. 

For someone from a non-religious Western household, it's a very different experience to see death being handled so openly and publicly. In Australian, ceremonies are usually far more private, with most of the preparation work done behind the scenes. The way it is a normal part of the Nepalese culture was interesting to see - there were local kids diving for coins in the water while bodies were being dunked in to be cleansed, as well as families sitting on the opposite side of the riverbank having a picnic while watching some of the ceremonies. 

I was glad to have a guide for the experience.  I usually decline guides, but had heard they are good to have to explain the ceremonies.  I didn't have to search for one, since one greeted me at the booth where I paid my entrance fee. The guide took us to a quieter spot on the opposite side of the river, from where we watched one of the cremation ceremonies. He explained each part of the process, gave interesting cultural, spoke to me about some interesting Nepalese history and answered my many questions. I paid him 1,000 rupees, which seems to be the going rate and I thought was very reasonable given he spent almost an hour with me, gave some great insights and so patiently answered my questions! 

For me this was one of the highlights from my visit to Kathmandu.

results.title: Interesting and Totally Different
results.text:
I regret that my visit was very brief as I was on a private tour with a driver and covering three other tourist sites. It's best to come early in order to cover the whole area. It's both very interesting and totally different to the West. The entrance fee is 1000 Rupees. 

BEWARE the self licensed guide at the booking office!!! He stands there and behaves as though he is part of the Pashupatinath Temple but infact he is NOT. He starts talking to you and follows you in and later informs you that you can pay him a contribution for his efforts!! AND even asks you for your ticket!!!
